domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer, so 1/n is well-defined and positive
j is an integer constrained by 0 <= j <= n minus 1
the affine map is defined on the half-open interval [0, 1/n)
the codomain/target is the interval I_{n,j}
the inverse formula x maps from I_{n,j} back to [0, 1/n)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n and every integer j with 0 <= j <= n minus 1, define J_{n,j} from [0, 1/n) to I_{n,j} by J_{n,j}(d) equals j/n plus d. Then J_{n,j} is a bijection onto I_{n,j}, and the inverse function is: given x in I_{n,j}, the corresponding preimage is d equals x minus j/n.
quantifier_order: for a fixed positive integer n
for a fixed integer j satisfying 0 <= j <= n minus 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: parameter of the family of maps and intervals; determines scale 1/n

variables.name: j
variables.role: parameter indexing the target interval I_{n,j}; determines translation by j/n

variables.name: d
variables.role: input variable to the affine map J_{n,j}

variables.name: x
variables.role: input variable to the inverse map

witness_dependencies: the map J_{n,j} depends on both n and j through the translation term j/n
the claimed inverse x minus j/n depends on j (and implicitly on n via the target interval I_{n,j})

statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. The affine map J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d is a bijection from [0, 1/n) onto I_{n,j}; its inverse is x -> x - j/n.
